# <span style="color:#E656AE;">Guerilla Analytics</span>

When working with a lot of data-files, it is essential to keep all these files organized in order to have a structured data analysis workflow framework.To build this kind of framework, I used the <span style="color:#E656AE;font-weight:bold;">Guerrilla Analytics</span>. 

While using the Guerrilla analytics, I kept the 7 principles of this method in mind:

1. Space is cheap, confusion is expensive

2. Use simple, visual project structures and conventions

3. Automate with program code

4. Link stored data to data in the analytics environment to data in work products 

5. Version control changes to data and analytics code (Git/Github.com)

6. Consolidate team knowledge (agree on guidelines and stick to it as a team)

7. Use code that runs from start to finish



---


For the past course, DAUR-II, I created a lot of files.
The DAUR-II course let me work on how to analyse two real biological sets of data: <span style="color:#E656AE;font-weight:bold;">RNA-sequencing data</span> and <span style="color:#E656AE;font-weight:bold;">metagenomics data</span>.

When organizing my RNA-sequencing data files (*Figure 1.*), I have first created <span style="color:#E656AE;font-weight:bold;">"README.txt"</span> text files. These README files provide the essential information about a project. 
For the RNA-sequencing data this included the different types of methods that were used to pre(process) and essential packages to install etc.

Following the README.txt we have a folder called <span style="color:#E656AE;font-weight:bold;">"data"</span>. This folder contains all data processing files categorized in subfolders and a special folder for all figures. 

![**<span style="color:#E656AE; font-style:italic;">Figure 1. Folder tree for the RNA-sequencing data</span>**](~/bookdown/photos/RNAseq_folder_tree.png)

---


For organizing the metagnomics data files (*Figure 2.*) the same structure has been made for the folder tree as the RNA-sequencing analyses. The only important addition to this tree is the folder for the final versions of my Rmarkdowns. My final version was named under "Meta.Rmd" in the folder "v2".     

![<span style="color:#E656AE; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic;">Figure 2. Folder tree for the metagnomics data</span>](~/bookdown/photos/metagenomics_folder_tree.png)
